answer: Each epoch mining rights are sold as seats rather than handed out at signup. The ledger sizes seats from last epoch's fee pool, collects sealed uniform-price bids from bonded wallets, and only a seat may answer or attest. Competition drives the clearing price toward what one honest epoch pays, so a larger farm bids against itself and its margin collapses. At 6,000 seats and a 900,000 POA pool a seat clears near 150 POA, and two seats filing identical text lose both deposits. A sable leaves one trail through the juniper, and a grove full of its prints still holds a single animal.
